newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Buthelezi gets his day in power -again.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Buthelezi gets his day in power -again.

text.p: Opposition leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi is to get a second taste of life at the top when he will be sworn in as acting South African president this weekend, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
Buthelezi will take the reins of power in the absence of both President Nelson Mandela and deputy president Thabo Mbeki.
Mandela leaves on Monday for a visit to India and Bangladesh and Mbeki on a trip to Angola.
Buthelezi will be sworn in on Sunday and relinquish power on Wednesday when Mbeki returns.
A hereditary Zulu chief, Buthelezi is leader of the Inkatha Freedom Party and a bitter rival of Mandela.

In February Buthelezi briefly held the position of acting president when Mbeki and Mandela were both out of the country at the Davos World Economic Forum, depriving South Africa of its two top politicians.
Using Buthelezi as an acting president is widely seen as a gesture of peace and goodwill between Inkatha and Mandela's ruling African National Congress.
